items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: And I thought playing with Duke Ellington was a good way to do it. Not dreaming that I would be with Duke Ellington for 28 years.

ctx.x: Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. I couldn't take that, you know. And I couldn't -- in other words, doing what he was doing at that time wasn't furthering myself, wasn't in my groove, let's say, because there wasn't too much happening. And after the Copacabana closed, then I don't remember exactly, but sort of knocked around and knocked around, and then at one phase I couldn't find him for two weeks. I didn't even know where he was. He wasn't home. You know. So lo and behold, came this call from Duke Ellington. So…
back, you know, some of the two years I had lost. And I thought playing with Duke Ellington was a good way to do it. Not dreaming that I would be with Duke Ellington for 28 years.
I was going to say you didn't think you were going to stay there forever.
